display.title: Episode 3: The Tall Chanukah Candles (Chanukah)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi's Chanukah show: what the word mitzvah really means, Chanukah songs with a studio guest, and the story of a Chassid saved from robbers by three-foot-tall Chanukah candles.
display.summary_long: Broadcast during Chanukah 5742. Uncle Yossi answers a listener's letter asking what "mitzvah" means: a mitzvah is a commandment from Hashem, our Commander-in-Chief, and that is what Chanukah is about, since the Greeks were happy for Jews to do "good deeds" but not to call them G-d's commandments. Each Chanukah light also kindles a spark in our soul to fight the yetzer hara. A studio guest then leads Chanukah songs in Hebrew, English and Yiddish, including Maoz Tzur and "I Have a Little Dreidel". After the sponsor and the Shema, story time tells of Naftali, a joyful Chassid whom the Rebbe Rashab told to buy Chanukah candles three feet tall. Stranded in a blizzard and caught by robbers, he lights them on top of his wagon; firemen in a distant watchtower see the flames, ride to the spot and the robbers flee. That is why Naftali dances on Chanukah. The show closes with Dial-a-Jewish-Story and the children's Sefer Torah.
display.lesson: We do mitzvos because Hashem commanded them, and following a tzaddik's instructions with joy brings Hashem's miracles.
